data.name: Learn.blinds.Summary
data.value: Forced bets, who pays them and who acts first.

data.name: Learn.blinds.s1
data.value: So every hand is worth something, there are two forced bets – the blinds. D is the dealer button. To its left the small blind (SB) pays a small bet, the next player the big blind (BB) – usually twice as much.

data.name: Learn.blinds.s2
data.value: After every hand the button moves one seat to the left. That way everyone pays the blinds in turn.

data.name: Learn.blinds.s3
data.value: The button is here. Click the player who pays the big blind.

data.name: Learn.blinds.s3.Explain
data.value: The big blind sits two seats to the left of the button.

data.name: Learn.blinds.s4
data.value: Blinds 10/20. How much do you have to pay at least before the flop to play?

data.name: Learn.blinds.s4.Explain
data.value: To play you have to pay at least the big blind – 20 here.

data.name: Learn.blinds.s5
data.value: Before the flop the player to the left of the big blind starts. The blinds act last – they've already put something in. The numbers show the order.

data.name: Learn.blinds.s6
data.value: Who has to act first before the flop here?

data.name: Learn.blinds.s6.Explain
data.value: The seat directly left of the big blind – “under the gun” – starts before the flop. Here that's you!

data.name: Learn.blinds.s7
data.value: Special case heads-up (only two players): the button pays the small blind. It acts first before the flop and last after it.

data.name: Learn.positions.Summary
data.value: Why acting last is an advantage.

data.name: Learn.positions.s1
data.value: After the flop the first player left of the button always starts. The button acts last. Acting last is a big advantage: you see what everyone else does before you decide.

data.name: Learn.positions.s2
data.value: That's why seats are grouped into positions: Early – right after the blinds. You need strong hands here. Late – just before and on the button. You can play more hands here. Blinds – first to act after the flop, a tough spot.

data.name: Learn.positions.s3
data.value: Who acts last after the flop?

data.name: Learn.positions.s3.Explain
data.value: The button – where the D is.

data.name: Learn.positions.s4
data.value: And who acts first after the flop if everyone is still in?

data.name: Learn.positions.s4.Explain
data.value: The small blind to the left of the button starts after the flop.

data.name: Learn.positions.s5
data.value: You're in early position with 7♣ 2♦ – the weakest starting hand. What's usually right?

data.name: Learn.positions.s5.Explain
data.value: With weak cards in early position, better fold – many players after you can still raise.

data.name: Learn.positions.s6
data.value: You're on the button and everyone before you folded. You have A♥ K♥. What's a good idea?

data.name: Learn.positions.s6.Explain
data.value: Strong hand and the best position: raise! That builds the pot and puts you in control.

data.name: Learn.positions.s7
data.value: Done – you now know the basics! At the practice table you can try everything risk-free. The tips show your chance of winning.

data.name: Learn.ranking.Summary
data.value: Which hand beats which? With exercises to compare.

data.name: Learn.ranking.s1
data.value: In Texas Hold'em you get 2 cards of your own. Up to 5 community cards lie in the middle and belong to everyone. Your hand is always the best 5 cards out of those 7. The glowing cards show your best hand.

data.name: Learn.ranking.s2
data.value: These are all the hands – from strongest to weakest. The rarer a hand, the more it's worth. No need to memorise them right away: in the game you'll always find the list under “🃏 Hands”.

data.name: Learn.ranking.s3
data.value: Who wins? Think about the best 5 cards each player can make with the cards in the middle.

data.name: Learn.ranking.s4
data.value: Straight against flush – which is worth more?

data.name: Learn.ranking.s5
data.value: Both have a pair of aces. What decides now?

data.name: Learn.ranking.s5.Explain
data.value: With the same hand the highest side card – the “kicker” – decides: king beats queen.

data.name: Learn.ranking.s6
data.value: And here? Look closely at the middle.

data.name: Learn.ranking.s6.Explain
data.value: The best hand is entirely in the middle: an ace-high straight. Both play it – the pot is split.

data.name: Learn.ranking.s7.Explain
data.value: A full house beats a flush – it's rarer.

data.name: Learn.rounds.Summary
data.value: Preflop, flop, turn, river – and what you can do in each round.

data.name: Learn.rounds.s1
data.value: A hand has up to four betting rounds. Before each round new cards come to the middle. Preflop: you only see your 2 cards. The first betting round starts.

data.name: Learn.rounds.s2
data.value: Flop: three community cards at once. Second betting round. You only need an eight or a king for a straight.

data.name: Learn.rounds.s3
data.value: Turn: the fourth card. Third betting round. The eight arrives – straight!

data.name: Learn.rounds.s4
data.value: River: the fifth and last card. Last betting round. Showdown: whoever is still in shows their cards. The best hand wins the pot.

data.name: Learn.rounds.s5
data.value: In every betting round you have these options: Check – bet nothing (only if nobody has bet yet). Bet – put chips into the pot. Call – pay an opponent's bet. Raise – bet more than the opponent. Fold – give up. Your chips in the pot are gone.

data.name: Learn.rounds.s6
data.value: Nobody has bet in this round yet. What can you NOT do?

data.name: Learn.rounds.s6.Explain
data.value: You can only call when someone has bet before. Without a bet you can check or bet.

data.name: Learn.rounds.s7
data.value: An opponent bets 40 and you fold. What happens to your chips already in the pot?

data.name: Learn.rounds.s7.Explain
data.value: What's in the pot belongs to the pot. Folding costs nothing extra – but you can't win the hand any more.

data.name: Learn.rounds.s8
data.value: We play no-limit. How much can you bet at most?

data.name: Learn.rounds.s8.1
data.value: As much as is in the pot

data.name: Learn.rounds.s8.Explain
data.value: No-limit means you can bet everything at any time. But from each opponent you win at most as much as you put in yourself.
